messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean,

This should work:

library(doParallel)
library(NicheMapR)

caribbean.points<- matrix(data = c(rep(140, 3), rep(-35, 3)), nrow = 3, ncol = 2)

cl<-makeCluster(3)
registerDoParallel(cl)

foreach(i = 1:nrow(caribbean.points), .verbose=F, .packages=c("NicheMapR")) %dopar% {

  micro = micro_global(loc=caribbean.points[i,], nyears=1, timeinterval = 12)

  nyears = micro$nyears
  maxshades = micro$MAXSHADES
  REFL = micro$REFL
  DEP = micro$DEP
  metout = micro$metout
  shadmet = micro$shadmet
  soil = micro$soil
  shadsoil = micro$shadsoil
  soilmoist = micro$soilmoist
  shadmoist = micro$shadmoist
  humid = micro$humid
  shadhumid = micro$shadhumid
  soilpot = micro$soilpot
  shadpot = micro$shadpot
  RAINFALL = micro$RAINFALL
  ectoin = rbind(as.numeric(micro$ALTT), as.numeric(micro$REFL)[1],
    micro$longlat[1], micro$longlat[2])

  ecto<-ectotherm(nyears = nyears, REFL = REFL, DEP = DEP, maxshades = maxshades,
    metout = metout, shadmet = shadmet, soil = soil, shadsoil = shadsoil,
    soilmoist = soilmoist, shadmoist = shadmoist, humid = humid, shadhumid = shadhumid,
    soilpot = soilpot, shadpot = shadpot, RAINFALL = RAINFALL, ectoin = ectoin)

  yearoutput<-cbind(caribbean.points[1,1],caribbean.points[1,2],ecto$environ)
  write.table(yearoutput, file ="yearoutput.csv", sep = ",", col.names = F, qmethod = "double", append = T)

}

stopCluster(cl)

All the best,
Mike

Thanks for another release of NicheMapR. I've tried testing the new soilgrids functionality in this release but get an error when soilgrids=1:

Any ideas what may be wrong? I think the SoilGrids database is being queried properly but the code seems to error at line 550 in NicheMapR::micro_global.

I have tried to troubleshoot given your point 2 above but the link to the SoilGrids tutorial is dead so I can't follow this through.I'd be happy to specify the soil moisture property vectors (PE, KS, BB, BD) manually but I don't know what all of these arguments stand for (I think BD = Bulk Density, KS = saturated hydraulic conductivity). Are there some global rasters for each of these parameters that I can download, in order to extract the values at each cell centroid?

I'm running NicheMapR 1.1.4 on Windows 10.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Sadly SoilGrids has stopped working for me. I'm still seeing what might be going wrong. But in the meantime, you can just specify your own soil hydraulic properties like this (based on the data in Campbell and Norman's table 9.1):

library(NicheMapR)
CampNormTbl9_1
          Texture Silt Clay airentry   b      Ks field wilting
1             sand 0.05 0.03      0.7 1.7 5.8e-03  0.09    0.03
2       loamy sand 0.12 0.07      0.9 2.1 1.7e-03  0.13    0.06
3       sandy loam 0.25 0.10      1.5 3.1 7.2e-04  0.21    0.10
4             loam 0.40 0.18      1.1 4.5 3.7e-04  0.27    0.12
5        silt loam 0.65 0.15      2.1 4.7 1.9e-04  0.33    0.13
6  sandy clay loam 0.13 0.27      2.8 4.0 1.2e-03  0.26    0.15
7        clay loam 0.34 0.34      2.6 5.2 6.4e-05  0.32    0.20
8  silty clay loam 0.58 0.33      3.3 6.6 4.2e-05  0.37    0.32
9       sandy clay 0.07 0.40      2.9 6.0 3.3e-05  0.34    0.24
10      silty clay 0.45 0.45      3.4 7.9 2.5e-05  0.39    0.25
11            clay 0.20 0.60      3.7 7.6 1.7e-05  0.40    0.27

soiltype <- 10 # choose a silty clay
BulkDens <- 1 # Mg/m3 peat bog (can go up to .01)
Density <- 2.56 # Mg/m3
PE<-vector() # create empty vector
KS<-vector() # create empty vector
BB<-vector() # create empty vector
BD<-vector() # create empty vector
PE[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,4] #air entry potential J/kg
KS[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,6] #saturated conductivity, kg s/m3
BB[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,5] #soil 'b' parameter
BD[1:19]<-BulkDens # soil bulk density value for soil moisture calcs (Mg/m3)
DD <- rep(Density, 19)

micro<-micro_global(BulkDens = BulkDens, Density = Density, PE = PE, KS = KS, BB = BB, BD = BD, DD = DD)

But note that you should run it for a daily time step if you're interested in soil moisture (which is what these properties are form) and have a year 'spin-up' to let the soil moisture settle down from the initial conditions. E.g.

micro<-micro_global(timeinterval = 365, nyears = 2, BulkDens = BulkDens, Density = Density, PE = PE, KS = KS, BB = BB, BD = BD, DD = DD)

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: micro_USA() function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam,

Very sorry this has taken so long. I've fixed the problem - it seems that there was a change in the netCDF file setup where the order of latitude and longitude was switched. It should work now. Note, however, that with R v3.5 the ncdf4 version from https://github.com/pmjherman/r-ncdf4-build-opendap-windows doesn't seem to work any longer :(.

Thanks for alerting me to the problem!

All the best,
Mike

p.s. it's easy to download the grids if you have the local storage space, and then your queries to the data will be faster: http://www.climatologylab.org/gridmet.html
